en: O God Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice;
impel the lord of the sacrifice for the sake of fortune.
The divine Gandharva, the purifier of intentions, shall purify our intention;
may the Lord of Speech make our speech sweet. O Desire, we know your name; you are named Rapture.
I have brought together that [essence]; it became your surā. Here, however, you were fashioned from the fire of birth and ascetic heat. Svāhā! Svāhā! I unite this seat of yours with honey.
This is the second mouth of Prajāpati.
By it, O woman, you shall overcome all men; you are the sovereign queen who brings the unsubmissive under your control. Svāhā! 3.
The ancient seers, concealing themselves, made Agni the consumer of raw flesh;
they made him the sacrificial butter for Tvaṣṭṛ’s three-horned [offering] within the womb of women.

May those goddesses clothe you with old age;
O long-lived one, put on this garment. Clothe her, clothe her with a garment.
Make her one who lives a hundred years; grant her long life. Live for a hundred autumns, full of luster, and while living, distribute wealth among the noble.
Soma gave [it] to the Gandharva;
the Gandharva gave it to Agni; he gave both wealth and sons.
May Agni [protect] this for me;
may my path, as I go forth, be prepared, auspicious, and free from harm, so that I may go to the world of my husband.
May the path leading away from her be prepared;
may she go to the world of her husband, auspicious and unharmed.
May Agni go first among the deities.
May he release her offspring from the noose of death.
May King Varuṇa grant his consent that this woman may not weep over the misfortune of losing a grandson. Svāhā! 10
May Agni Gārhapatya protect the boundary;
may he grant her offspring a full lifespan. May she be a mother whose lap is never empty of living children.
May she realize the bliss of her grandson; Svāhā! 11 May Vāyu protect your back today, and may the Aśvins protect your thighs.
May Savitṛ protect the sons until they are weaned;
may Bṛhaspati protect them until the putting on of the garment; may the Viśvedevas protect them from behind. Svāhā! 12
Let your cry at night arise only in your own house;
let those who weep for you gather elsewhere.
Do not, weeping, press upon our chest.
O wife of a living husband, shine forth in the world of your husband, beholding your offspring with a joyful mind. Svāhā!
May there be the death of your grandson while you still have progeny. 13.
Having cast off evil or distress like a garland from one's head, I fasten this bond upon my enemies. Svāhā! 14
May death depart; may immortality come to me.
May Vaivasvata grant us fearlessness.
O Death, go along the further path!
Where there is no other besides us on the path of the gods—to you who possess sight and hear, I speak this: do not harm our progeny, nor our heroes. Svāhā! 15.15.151.
Ascend this stone;
like a stone, be thou firm.
Drive away the one who hates us.
And may you not fall beneath the power of enemies; this woman speaks thus as she scatters parched grain into the fire.
May my husband be long-lived;
may he live for a hundred years; may my kinsmen prosper. Svāhā! 2
The maidens have now worshipped the divine Aryaman and Agni; may that divine Aryaman [accept] her.
May Pūṣan release me from here; svāhā! 3. Now the maidens have worshipped the god Pūṣan and Agni.
May that divine Pūṣan, who has gone forth, release me from here; Svāhā! 4.
As a maiden going to the world of her husband from her fathers—
Yama performed this initiation;
O maiden, may we, through you, overcome our enemies as one crosses flowing streams of water. 5
May Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of food; may Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of strength;
may Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of the vow.
May Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of the fourfold prosperity;
may Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of offspring and cattle;
may Viṣṇu lead you for the sake of the increase of wealth.
May Viṣṇu lead you to the seven *hotrā*s from the seven;
become my companion of seven steps, may I attain your friendship.
Do not fail me in friendship; may you not fail me in friendship. 13 This bride is most auspicious.
Look upon her together with this [husband];
having bestowed good fortune upon her, go back to your homes from here. 14
May all the gods be in harmony;
may the waters be in harmony between our two hearts;
may Mātariśvan be in harmony, and may Dhātṛ be in harmony.
May she, the uniter, bestow [this] upon us both. I grasp your hand for the sake of good fortune,
so that you may reach old age with me as your husband.
Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Puraṃdhi— the gods have given you to me for the status of mistress of the household.
O woman with the keen eye, be one who does not bring ill fortune to her husband.

Auspicious to the animals, well-disposed, full of luster, mother of heroes, mother of living sons, loving the gods—be gracious, O gentle one; bring welfare to our bipeds and welfare to our quadrupeds. 17
May Prajāpati produce offspring for us; may Aryaman anoint us for old age.
Free from ill fortune, enter the world of your husband.
Be auspicious to our bipeds, be auspicious to our quadrupeds.
O bounteous Indra, make this boundary-line well-provided with sons and fortunate.
Bestow upon her ten sons;
make her husband the eleventh. Be a sovereign queen over your father-in-law.
Be a sovereign queen over your mother-in-law;
be a sovereign queen over your sister-in-law;
be a sovereign queen over your brothers-in-law. 20
May your heart be placed within my vow;
may your mind follow my mind. With a single-minded focus, take pleasure in my word.
May Bṛhaspati bind you to me. 21. 2.
Those [marks] of yours which are at the junctions of the lines, in the eyelashes, and in the curls—
All those evils in your hair, as well as whatever evil is elsewhere, I pacify for you with this full oblation.
Whatever occurred when you were looked upon and when you wept— all those I pacify for you with this final oblation.
Whatever evil there is in your conduct,
in your speech, and in your laughter—
may all that be consumed by this full oblation.
I pacify all [afflictions] that are in the eye-sockets, the teeth, the hands, and the feet. 3.
All of these I pacify for you with the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti):
those in the thighs, the private parts, and the shanks.
And those [faults] of yours that exist during the junctions— those I pacify for you all with the final oblation.
Whatever terrible afflictions there were in all your limbs,
they were [removed] by the oblations of clarified butter.
I have stilled all those [calamities]:
firm is the sky, firm is the earth,
and firm is this entire world.
Firm are these mountains;
firm is this woman in her husband's family,
bound by the jewel-noose of food.
With the breath-thread, with the speckled one,
with the knot of truth, I bind together your mind and your heart.
That which is this heart of yours, let that be my heart;
that which is this heart of mine—
Let that heart of yours be subdued by the sixty parts of breath;
with that I bind you, O [Name].
Upon the *śuṣka*, the *śuka*, the *śalmali*, the multiform, the golden-colored, the well-fashioned,
the fair-wheeled— ascend, O Sūryā, to the navel of immortality.
Prepare a pleasant bridal procession for the husband; let not waylayers who lie in wait find the couple.
Having crossed over the difficult passage by easy means, let the enemies flee; O cows, beget offspring! 12. O lions, beget offspring!
Here are the horses, here the men;
let Pūṣan too, who bestows a thousand sacrificial fees, sit down here. 13
O lion, here is steadfastness, here is self-restraint, here is delight; take your pleasure here.
In me is steadfastness, in me is self-restraint.
Delight in me; delight in me.
14.3 O Agni, in the expiation, you are the expiation of the gods.
I, a Brahmin seeking a protector, approach you;
drive away that evil fortune which belongs to her.
O Vāyu, you are the expiation among the gods;
I, a Brāhmaṇa seeking protection, approach you for refuge.
O Moon, in this expiation, drive away that body of hers which is fatal to her husband. 2.
O Moon, in this expiation.
You are the atonement for the gods.
I, a Brāhmaṇa desiring protection, approach you.
That body of hers which is childless—
Drive away that which belongs to Tamas. O Surya, you are the expiation of the gods; you are the expiation.
I, a Brāhmaṇa seeking protection, approach you;
whatever part of her body is unfavorable to cattle, drive that away from her. 4.
O Agni, Vāyu, Candra, and Sūrya, you are the expiations;
you are the expiations of the gods.
I, a Brāhmaṇa desiring protection, approach you for refuge.
Whatever ill fortune she has, whatever brings destruction to her husband,
whatever brings destruction to her sons, and whatever brings destruction to her cattle— drive all that away from her.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb;
may Tvaṣṭṛ shape the forms;
may Prajāpati pour [the seed].
May Dhātṛ place the embryo within you;
O Sinīvālī, bestow the embryo;
O Sarasvatī, bestow the embryo.
May the two divine Aśvins, wreathed with lotuses, place the embryo within you; may Mitra and Varuṇa grant you a male child.
Both Aśvins are male;
Agni and Vāyu are male;
the embryo within your womb is male. 8.
A man is Agni, a man is Indra;
a man is the god Bṛhaspati.
As a man, may you obtain a son.
May a man be born after him.
9.4 This tree is full of vigor; be full of vigor and bear fruit.
O leaf, O lord of the forest,
may wealth be bestowed upon you;
by which [leaf] one leads to the boundary of Aditi.
Prajāpati [bestows this] for great good fortune.
With that, I lead her to the boundary;
I make her offspring reach old age. 2
May Rākā, who is easily invoked, be well-praised; may she hear us, the fortunate one, and take notice of us by herself.
May she sew together the openings with a needle that does not break.
May she grant a hero, foremost of whom is one who lives a hundred years.
O Rākā, those well-formed favors of yours, by which you bestow riches upon the donor—
With those [rays], come to us today with a gracious mind,
O fortunate one, bestowing thousandfold prosperity.
What do you see?
May she who lies across bestow upon me offspring, cattle, good fortune,
and long life for my husband.
"I am Vidharaṇī.
As such, I worship you with a stream of clarified butter; may I be successful in my attainment.
To the goddess Samrādhanī, the director,
Vipaścit brought the tail;
Dhātṛ brought it back again.
By others, however, you will be born as this wise man named Asau.
This is the command; this is food; this is life; this is immortality.
May Mitra and Varuṇa grant you wisdom.
May Agni bestow wisdom upon you;
may the two divine Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, grant you wisdom. 9
O fair-limbed one, that which is placed within your heart, within Prajāpati—
I know it; I consider that to be Brahman.
May I not incur the sin of a grandson;
may that which is immortal on earth and rests in the moon in heaven [be mine].
I have taken the name of the nectar of the Vedas;
may I not suffer the sin of my grandson.
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection.
O Prajāpati,
grant offspring for me, so that this son may not die before his mother’s sight.
There is a black spot in the moon,
resting upon the heart of the earth;
knowing that and beholding it, I am wise.
May I not weep for the sin of a grandson.
Thou art a thunderbolt; which one art thou?
This one is thee; thou art immortal.
May he enter the month presided over by Bṛhaspati;
may day entrust you to night, and may night entrust you to day.
May Night entrust you to Day and Night; may Day and Night entrust you to the fortnights;
may the fortnights entrust you to the months.
May the months entrust you to the seasons;
may the seasons entrust you to the year; may the year entrust you to life and old age, O so-and-so! 15
From limb after limb you are born, from the heart you arise;
I join your breath with my breath.
Live with me for as long as life lasts. You arise from every limb; you are born from the heart.
"Veda indeed is the name of your son;
live for a hundred autumns! Be a stone, be an axe! (17)
Become gold that is spread out.
You are the self, my son; do not die. Live for a hundred autumns. 18
I smell you with the *hiṅkāra* of the spies, O [Name]! 19.5 Savitṛ has come here with the razor.
Be warm with water, O Vāyu! 2.
May the waters moisten you for life. 3. You are the seat of Viṣṇu. 4. O herb, protect him! 5.
O Svadhitī, do not harm him!
With that [blade] with which Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati,
Vāyu, and Indra sowed [the seed].
With that sacred word (*brahman*), I anoint you for life, for living, for long life, and for splendor—
[the triple life-span] of Jamadagni.
The triple life-span of Kaśyapa, the triple life-span of Agastya, the triple life-span of the gods—
May that be yours for a triple life-span.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow;
I declare it unto you.
May I be able to do that; may I succeed through it. Here I go from untruth to truth. Svāhā! O Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow. Svāhā! 9.
O Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow.
I declare that to you; may I be able to do it, and may I prosper thereby. From untruth I go to truth. Svāhā! 10
O Sūrya, lord of vows, I shall perform the vow; I declare it to you. May I be able to do it, and may I prosper through it.
"Here I go from untruth to truth; Svāhā!
O Moon, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow;
I declare this to you."
May I be able to do that; may I succeed through it. "Here I go from untruth to truth. Svāhā!
O Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow of those who observe vows."
That I declare to you; may I be able to do it, and may I prosper thereby. From untruth I go unto truth. Svāhā! 13.
We have come together with the non-comer;
keep the mortal away from us. May we move about unharmed.
May there be well-being for this one who moves about.
Savitṛ has taken your hand; Agni has taken your hand.
Aryaman took your hand;
you are Mitra by deed; Agni is your teacher. 15.
"Come to me for the practice of celibacy (brahmacarya). What is your name? My name is so-and-so. In the impulse of the divine Savitṛ..."
With the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take your hand, O [Name]! 18. Follow the turning of the Sun, O [Name]! 19.
You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not loosen! O Antaka, I entrust this person to you.
O Sahuri, I entrust this person to you. 20–21.
O Skṛśana, I entrust this one to you, [name]. 22. O Prajāpati, I entrust [name] to you. 23. O God Savitṛ, I entrust [name] to you. 24.
"O student of sacred knowledge (brahmacārin), place fuel on the fire; drink water;
perform your duties; do not sleep during the day."
Sītā has come to me, driving away ill-spoken words, purifying my pure complexion,
and bringing strength through the out-breath and the in-breath.
This auspicious goddess is my girdle;
she is the protector of what has flowed, the one who reaches beyond ascetic heat, striking down the Rakṣas and overcoming the enemies.
Go around me on all sides, O auspicious one;
may we not come to harm through your girdle, O supporter. 28.
That excellent splendor of Savitṛ...
We meditate upon the splendor of the divine;
may he inspire our intellects.
29 Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om. 30
O you of good fame, make me one of good fame;
as you are of good fame among the gods, O you of good fame, so may I be of good fame among the Brahmins. 31
I have brought a fuel-stick for Agni,
the great Jātavedas;
just as you, O Agni, are kindled by the fuel-stick.
Thus may I prosper in life-span, in wisdom, in luster, in progeny, in cattle, in the splendor of sacred knowledge, in wealth, and in food; svāhā!
May power come to me from my kinsmen.
May life return; may fortune return;
may wealth return to me;
may the Brahminhood return to me. 33
May my mind come back to me; may my breath, my eye, and my ear come back to me.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceivable protector of the body, [protect me].
May my mind, the banner of immortality, abide within; Svāhā! 34. 6 Those fires that have entered into the waters—Gohya, Upagohya, Marūka, and Manohā—[to them be homage].
The wicked one, the destroyer, the emaciated defiler, the seizer of the senses— these I cast away from here.
Whatever of the waters is terrible, whatever of the waters is cruel.
Whatever is unappeased in me, that I cast away; that which is radiant, that I take here;
with that, I consecrate myself. 3.
For glory, for splendor, for sacred luster, for strength,
for sensory power, for heroism, for the enjoyment of food, for the increase of wealth, for brilliance, and for honor. 4.
With that [power] by which you two made a woman, with which you two touched the surā liquor,
and with which you two sprinkled the dice.
O Aśvins, with that glory by which you [traversed] this great earth, with that [glory],
sprinkle me. 5.
Indra has mounted with the Maruts who possess gleaming spears;
he has mounted with those who travel at dawn.
You are the winner of ten; make me a winner of ten.
I enter you; enter me.
Rising up with his flaming spears, Indra has taken his stand with the Maruts; he has taken his stand with the Sāṃtapana Maruts.
O hundred-slayer, make me a hundred-slayer;
I enter you, let me enter you.
Rising up with his flaming spears, Indra has stood firm with the Maruts.
In the evening, with those [rays] by which thou hast stood, thou art a winner of a thousand; make me a winner of a thousand; I enter thee, enter me! 8.
You are the eye; you are the essence of sight. Strike away my evil. May King Soma protect you.
Salutations to you;
do not harm me. O Varuṇa, loosen the most excellent bond from us.
Having loosened [the bond] from the lowest and from the middle—then, O Āditya, under your law, may we be sinless before Aditi.
(10) You are glory; delight in me! (11)
O two eyes, you who are there, lead me [home]. 12. You are the Gandharva Upāvasu; protect me. 13. May I be dear to you as the eye is to the eye-ball. 14.
The mongoose has well-fitting covers;
the thunderbolt is measured by its teeth.
O tongue, do not be unsteady with speech!
O Lord of Sound, play here beautifully for our delight; may you be strong-limbed,
our friend, a deliverer, and a source of great heroism.
Bound with cow-hides, be firm;
may your rider win all that is to be won. 16.7 These [are] mine, O you of all-pervading power!
May Bhava and Indra protect you;
O Pūṣan, cause them to turn back— let those who have been lost return to our home.
These honey-sweet,
unerring cows, together with their milk, are the mothers of clarified butter.
May these cows be many here;
you are the phlegm of the cows,
may the cows cling to me.
Gather them up, gather them— those animals that are mine;
may Pūṣan grant them protection.
Just as those who are living have passed away,
you are the thousandfold world; O Indra, Sṛma gave you to me.
Unharmed, uninjured, and free from disease;
you are the nourisher of cattle, you rule over the nourishment of cattle; for the nourishment of cattle, I take you.
You are the nourisher of a thousandfold, you rule over a thousandfold nourishment.
For nourishment for a thousand years, I have made a pair for your ears with a red axe.
Of as many [women] as I have marked for you this year,
may there be even more of them for you.
May we perform the ritual action year after year.
This cord is the mother of the cows, the one who settles the calves.
"May she, rich in milk, yield for us in each succeeding year.
Thus ends the first section.
The second portion:
O King of Serpents, this which is in the eastern direction is your offering. 1.
O King of Serpents who is in the southern direction,
this is your offering.
O King of Serpents who is in the western direction...
This is your offering, O King of Serpents who is in the northern quarter;
this is your offering. 3–4.
Homage to the Earth!
To the tusked one, the sustainer of all! May we not be harmed at your end; strike together, do not strike apart.
Do not strike him; do not slay him! Soma is the king, Soma is the stalk-king, Soma is our king; we belong to Soma.
You are the destroyer of the Ahijambha; you are the pillar of Soma, the pillar of Soma is the destroyer of the Ahijambha. In that alliance which they established...
Together with the Seven Seers, O serpents, do not step upon us; homage be to you! Do not harm us. 7.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our own life; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroic sons in your wrath.
We, possessing oblations, ever invoke you—
the one who possesses a hundred weapons, a hundred powers, a hundred aids, and who overcomes adversaries.
May he who has lived for us a hundred autumns— may Indra lead us across all difficulties. Here are the four paths leading to the gods.
They spread out between heaven and earth;
O all you gods, grant him here to us who brings them freedom from defeat and freedom from exhaustion. 10
May summer, winter, spring, autumn,
and the rainy season be auspicious for us; may these seasons, through a hundred autumns, grant us prosperity.
May we be free from wind and fear among them. 11.
Offer great homage to the Sidhvatsara, the Parivatsara, and the Samvatsara.
May we, long-lived and unslain, abide in the good-will of those worthy of sacrifice.
O gods, you have led us from evil to greater prosperity.
May we be united with you through our devotion;
as a source of bliss, O Soma, enter us; be auspicious and gracious to our offspring and our bodies. Svāhā! 13
O Prāṇa, you are equal; I speak this truth: for you have entered into all things within. Having wiped away old age and disease from my body, [grant me health].
"Be for us, do not die, O Indra!
Let Agni eat first,
for he knows how the oblation is."
May Śivā, who dwells among all people, make the plants auspicious for us; Svāhā! 15.
That famous one, joined with honey and barley...
They ploughed upon the mind of Sarasvatī;
Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the plough, and the Maruts, the bounteous givers, were the ploughmen. Svāhā! 16.1
She, indeed, has shone forth at first; she became the milch-cow for Yama.
May she, rich in milk, yield her bounty for us.
Year after year,
I establish myself in sovereign power, I establish myself in the kingdom, I establish myself among the horses, and I establish myself among the cattle.

I establish myself in the vital breath, I establish myself in nourishment; I establish myself in the limbs, I establish myself in the self. 2. I establish myself in heaven and earth, I establish myself in the sacrifice. 3.
O Earth, be pleasant to us, thornless, and a place of rest;
grant us wide-spreading shelter.
"May [the gods] not [fear] me out of fear"—
thus did the animals reflect with their minds and their hearts.
With speech that has a thousand snares, I bind your mind; may your mother give her consent to you.
The father has followed, the brother, the uterine kinsman, the friend, and the fellow-herdsman have followed.
The oblation has been taken for the gods.
Whatever lowing a beast has uttered, or whatever it has struck with its feet,
may Agni deliver me from that sin.
May you release us from all [sins], O Haṃsa!
Agni has entered into Agni;
he is the son of the seers, this sovereign ruler.
May he, being gracious, sacrifice for us with a perfect sacrifice,
for he knows the generations of the gods.
The pressing-stones, together with the mortars, cry out aloud.
Preparing the oblation for the year-long rite,
O Ekāṣṭakā, may we live long with good offspring and brave sons, bringing offerings to you. 10
O Jātavedas, take up the oblations toward the seat of the Siddhas, which is crawling with serpents;
[take also] those domestic animals of manifold forms.
May there be delight for me in those seven. That very one who shone forth previously, she moves within the waters, having entered them.
The bride has won as the first progenitor, for within her are all powers of greatness;
she is indeed that same one who shone forth first.
She became a cow of every form;
she who is the consort of the year—may she be auspicious for us. 13
O gods, may you behold this night as she approaches like a cow;
may she yield for us milk in abundance.
Year after year, for each image of the year,
O Night, we worship you.
Make our progeny undecaying; unite us with the increase of wealth. May Anumati grant us this.
May the sacrifice be considered among the gods;
and may Agni, the bearer of oblations, grant happiness to us who offer it. 16.2
Svāhā to Soma accompanied by the ancestors!
Svāhā to Agni, the carrier of the *kavya* offerings!
Driven away are the Asuras and the Rakṣas who sit upon the sacrificial altar!
Those who, assuming various forms,
being Asuras, move about by means of their own inherent power,
and who carry away both distant forts and near ones— [may they be struck down].
May Agni drive those enemies away from this world.
Come, O Soma-loving fathers,
by your deep and ancient paths.
Wealth has been given to us here; O auspicious ones, bestow upon us riches consisting of all-heroic sons!
O fathers, rejoice here!
Drink according to your respective portions! 6.
The ancestors have rejoiced;
they have drunk according to their respective portions. 7.
Homage to you, O fathers, for life;
homage to you, O fathers, for vigor; homage to you, O fathers, for the terrible.
Homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of the essence;
homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of the svadhā offering; homage to you, O fathers, for the sake of wrath.
Homage to you, O fathers; fathers, homage to you!
11 Give us houses, O fathers; we give to you, O fathers, what is ever-present. 12
O Fathers, we have given you this garment; O Fathers, this is your garment. 13–14.
Carrying the sun, you are nectar, clarified butter, milk, sweet drink, and flowing liquor; you are the ancestral offering (svadhā).
Satisfy my ancestors! 15
O Fathers, bestow upon us a child, a boy adorned with a lotus wreath,
so that there may be a man here. 16
Jātavedas, our messenger, has carried the oblations; having made the offerings fragrant,
he presented them to the ancestors, who have eaten them with the *svadhā* call.
Knowing this, O Agni, return again to your source; Svāhā! O Jātavedas, [offer] the omentum to the fathers where you know them to be placed, gone far away.
May streams of fat flow toward them;
may their blessings and desires come true—svāhā!
O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum.
For you indeed became the first Hotṛ; may my offering of fat be accepted as true;
may that which I do here come to fulfillment for me. 19
Whatever debt I have incurred here through what was not given—
which causes me to wander under the dominion of Yama— by this, O Agni, I become free from that debt.
While still living, I give that back to you.
Sekāṣṭakā, performing austerities, gave birth to a child, Indra, who is greatness itself.
By means of that, the gods overcame their enemies;
he became the slayer of the Asuras through his powers.
21.3 We partake of this portion of the earth.
This, O auspicious one, is most propitious!
Drive away our rivals;
let the wealth of others fall to us.
He finds wealth for others.
Let us fashion this hymn with our intellect for Jātavedas, who is worthy of it, as one constructs a chariot.
For auspicious indeed is his providence for us;
O Agni, may we never suffer harm in your friendship. Let us bring fuel and prepare offerings for you.
Observing you at every joint, may we further our prayers for the sake of life;
O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm. 3.
May we be able to perfect thee with fuel; may our prayers be accomplished. In thee the gods eat the offered oblation. Bring hither the Ādityas, for we long for them.
O Agni, may we not suffer harm in your friendship. 4.
Ascetic heat, brilliance, faith, modesty, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, fortitude, and righteousness—these are yours.
I take refuge in existence, speech, mind, the self, and Brahman; may they protect me.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ.
I take refuge in the Great Self.
You are Virūpākṣa, the tooth-marked.
Your bed is upon a leaf; your home is in the intermediate space, a golden structure.
The hearts of the gods are contained within an iron jar;
Balabhr̥t and Balasā protect them with truth— unwavering, unblinking—
and so too do your twelve sons.
Having caused you to sacrifice with the Kāmapra sacrifice every year for twelve years, they enter again upon the life of a student.
You are a Brāhmaṇa among the gods; I am a Brāhmaṇa among men.
A Brahmin indeed pursues another Brahmin: "I pursue you!
Do not call out to me while I am chanting; do not offer on my behalf while I am offering oblations; do not act on my behalf while I am acting."
I take refuge in you; impelled by you, I shall perform this rite.
May it succeed for me; may it prosper for me; may it be accomplished for me.
May the ocean, the all-encompassing, authorize me through the sacred word (*brahman*).
May Tutha, the omniscient son of Brahmā, grant me permission; may Śvātra, the wise son of Mitra and Varuṇa, grant me permission.
To that Virūpākṣa, the conqueror with teeth, who is as all-pervading as the ocean—
Homage to Tutha, the all-knowing, the invigorating, the wise, the thousand-eyed son of Brahmā.
He has a thousand arms and is the lord of cattle.
May he protect the cattle;
may the Lord of Nourishment bestow nourishment upon me, and may the Lord of Progeny bestow progeny upon me. Svāhā! 7
The *kautumatī* plant makes my forest auspicious;
your mother is named *nākulī*.
I am composed of men.
O herb, join together for us that which of our desire has been severed. 8.
O Lord of the Earth, you stand like a tree bearing fruit;
to him who knows this, [grant] it for me.
O Great One, milk the enjoyments that are unimpaired;
the Soma is established in truth,
together with the past and the future.
May space descend upon me with food and prosperity;
you possess a share in all things.
All that is supported by you;
with all of that, O Vivāsan, do not drive me away, do not cause me to perish. 11
Like a treasury full of wealth, you joyfully bestow riches;
unseen, you bring about what is seen.
Grant me all desires.
This is the space of space which shines as this orb.
O God, he who knows you thus—
grant me the mastery over all things; bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om.
May I be like the sun for visibility, like fire in brilliance, like wind in breath,
like the moon in fragrance, and like Bṛhaspati in intelligence.
Like the two Aśvins in beauty, like Indra and Agni in strength—
may I indeed have a share of the *brahman*, and may my enemies have a share of evil. 14.4.14.4.
From my head, from Vaiśravaṇa, from those who have entered my skull,
and from my forehead, [arise] the terrible, devouring sounds.
I drive away your obstacles; Svāhā!
From my necks, from my shoulders, and from my nose, [I drive away] those who have entered within.
From my mouth, I speak; I drive away your terrible obstacles, svāhā! From my two arms, from wherever they may come, svāhā!
I drive away from your sides the fierce ones, and from your chest the terrible, cloud-like obstructors; Svāhā! (3)
From my groins, the blood-drinkers,
the womb-slayers, the Pajri-slayers, and from my thighs, the terrible Niśriṣas— [I drive them away].
I dispel your obstacles, svāhā!
4 From whatever direction they arise, from my two calves and from my two heels, I drive away those formidable ones.

I scatter the terrible ones at your feet; I drive away your obstacles. Svāhā! We worship the one who wards off [evil]. Svāhā! 5. We sacrifice to the one who surrounds [us]. Svāhā! 5. To him with long shanks and a speckled belly,
who afflicts us for the sake of giving and for the sake of procreation— svāhā! 6.
Depart from here, O oppressor; do not afflict me, nor cause me distress. Make a path easy for me to travel.
By which [path] he shall bring wealth to me; svāhā!
7 O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created beings.
Whatever desires we have for which we offer this oblation to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches. Svāhā!
8. May I become the glory of the Brahmins.
I am the glory of kings, the glory of the people, the glory of truth; I am the glory of glory. 9
May the deities come together, those who have departed from me; may they, the glorious and great ones, be present here in this golden vessel, the back of which is filled with Soma. 10
O Svarūpa, reveal your form to me;
I have consumed the food of the fierce splendor of your morning light.
"Let this indeed be in me, and let this be in you; let this be in you, and let this be in me. I see this with my own eyes."
What was given by you, O Prabhāsā—by that do not consume me; by that may I consume; by that enter into me.
May he carry us across the night; may he carry us across three times.
May the night carry us across;
may the day carry us across. O Āditya, I shall board the boat that is full and does not leak.
The flawless one! The one that carries across, with a hundred oars, for well-being! 14 To Sbhala, svāhā! 15
To Sbhallāya, svāhā! 16. O Vāstoṣpati, recognize us; be one who grants us easy entry and be free from disease for us.
Whatever we implore from you, accept that from us; be auspicious for our bipeds and auspicious for our quadrupeds.
O Rākā, O Sinīvālī!
O Sinīvālī, thick-haired one; O Subhadrā, Pathyā, Revatī:
bring us fame by way of the path. Svāhā! Svāhā! 2.
The paths that go eastward, those that have come from the north,
and all these paths that exist—
With those bring us glory! Svāhā!
3 As footprints follow, as months follow the revolving year;
Thus may the upholders of glory assemble from every side. Svāhā!
4 Just as the rivers [flow] into the ocean...
They come together from every direction.
In this way, may my companions, the students of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārin*), come together from every direction. Svāhā! 5
Be a winner of wealth, be a winner of wealth, be a winner of wealth!
You two are the subduers who go to the gods;
may all beings come under your control.
Thus may he come under my control. Svāhā! 7.
O Śaṅkha and Manaāyu, you two are the paths of the gods; as all beings come under your control, so [may he come under mine].
Thus may he come under my control. Svāhā! 8.
I approach the goddess Ākūti with my mind; she is the mother of sacrifice; may she be easy for me to invoke.
To her whose single syllable is supreme,
and whose branches are a thousand and ten thousand—
to that Vāc, I offer oblation in this invocation.
May prosperity and glory come to me. Svāhā! 9.
I, Siddha, offer this Viśvakarman Śrīvatsa into the fire. Svāhā! 10. I offer the full oblation for the sake of glory. Svāhā!
Whoever offers an oblation to him grants him a boon; I choose a boon: may I shine with glory in the world. Svāhā!
May the rivers flow for me.
Darkness is before you; I am light for you. May all of you come toward me. Svāhā! 12
Or, among the six, there is the state of having a single will, for one indeed causes the other beings to will the same. Svāhā!
13 This which is the *satvānaḥ* is indeed prosperity (*śrī*).
May Virocana bestow strength upon me. Svāhā! 14.
I offer clarified butter, which is indeed essence, desiring the perfection of splendor for the one who is seated. Svāhā! 15.
To hunger, svāhā! 16. To hunger and thirst, svāhā! 17.
Do not be afraid; you shall not die.
"You shall become one whose sight is impaired by old age;
I have not tasted the poison, for its mouth is like that of Ugrasphena. 18
O protector, guard me; O lord, guard me from curses and from enemies; you are the means of well-being. 19.6
Your worm has been slain by Atri;
your worm has been slain by Jamadagni;
it has been reduced to a blade of grass by Gotama.
Right here, O worm, I cut off your blameworthy speech with the mantra of Bharadvāja;
I cut you down, O worm! 2.
I drive away the worm that pierces crookedly,
the worm that moves within the intestines,
and the two-headed white worm.
The two-headed, four-jawed one is slain; O tiny worm, you are slain! Slain is the mother; slain is the father.
Now, their broken jar is that which contains poison for them;
O Indra, [seize] the worm with your two arms.
We cause them to fall headlong. 5.
The worms are slain, along with the *sāśātika* and the blue flies. 6–7. [This is] the *putravāsa* for the worthy one.
She became a cow for Yama;
may she, rich in milk, yield for us [milk] year after year.
Here I step upon this Virāj-foot for the sake of eating food:
those herbs whose king is Soma.
Many are you, possessing a hundredfold vision;
as such, grant me flawless protection upon this seat! 3.
Those herbs whose king is Soma, which are spread across the earth— may they [protect] me on this seat.
O you who are without flaw, grant us protection! From wherever I gaze upon you, O divine waters, from that very place may success come to me. 4–5.
I wash my left foot;
may I bestow prosperity upon this kingdom.
I wash my right foot.
I cause prosperity to enter this kingdom. 7. First one foot, then the other, I wash both feet for the sake of the kingdom’s prosperity and for the attainment of fearlessness. 8.
You are the sovereign of food;
may I become the sovereign.
You are glory; bestow glory upon me.
Thou art the glory of the glorious; thou art the food of the glorious;
thou art the food of the great.
You are the consumer of prosperity; bestow prosperity upon me! Svāhā! 12.
Release me from the noose of Varuṇa.
Speak to him who hates me; slay him, yet release the cow for both of us—let her eat grass and drink water. 13.
The daughter of the Rudras, the sister of the Vasus, the kinswoman of the Ādityas, the navel of immortality—
I proclaim her to the discerning person.
"Do not kill the cow, the non-going Aditi;
release her!
This is the second section.
